desk.headline: Revenue up 31% to $143.5m, beat; Q4 outlook points to first break-even adjusted EBITDA
results: Revenue grew 31% to $143.5m, ahead of the $137.9m estimate; US revenue rose 42%.
Adjusted gross margin edged up to 41% from 40%.
The net loss halved to $18.8m ($0.23 a share); the adjusted loss was close to zero.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.2m from $8.7m, though share-based pay doubled to $15.4m.
Operating cash outflow was $14.5m as customer receivables rose; cash ended at $322.8m.

guidance.summary: Via expects Q4 platform revenue of $150.0–151.7m (up 26–28%) and adjusted EBITDA of $0–1.5m, its first non-negative quarter. Full-year revenue is guided to $556.7–558.4m.

points: The sales pipeline more than doubled from a year ago to a record; large ‘network’ deals are seen as the main driver next year.
Management expects Q4 to be the first profitable quarter on adjusted EBITDA and adjusted earnings per share.
Management said full-year revenue guidance was raised; Germany ($18.4m) has stabilised but is not yet growing.
Over 95% of code is now written with AI, which management credits for margin gains and lower R&D costs.
A strong Israeli shekel cost about $5.4m of EBITDA this year; most Q4 exposure is hedged.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — Earnings Whispers, 9 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 delivers the first break-even or positive adjusted EBITDA quarter.
Cash flow, as government customers pay slowly and receivables rose in Q3.
Conversion of the record pipeline into large network deals, and a return to growth in Germany.
